article.core_task: Guide the reader to identify ripe crops, harvest standard crops by hand with platform controls (PC primary focus, holding right-click with cursor away to harvest underfoot), use a scythe on designated crop examples, harvest giant crops with an axe, ensure trellis crops are reachable, and troubleshoot harvest blockers.

sections.title: Introduction & Immediate Answer
sections.purpose: Provide the immediate, direct answer within the first three sentences: standard crops are harvested by hand (PC Right-Click / X), specific crops require a scythe (Left-Click / tool button), and giant crops require an axe.

sections.h2: How to Tell When Crops Are Ready to Harvest
sections.title: Recognizing Crop Readiness
sections.purpose: Instruct reader on identifying the final harvest stage sprite and calculating growth calendar days with watering rules.

subsections.h3: Visual Signs: Identifying the Final Harvest Stage Sprite
subsections.action: Check whether the crop has reached its final harvest stage sprite (as illustrated by mature Parsnip and Pumpkin stages). Fully grown crops display their mature sprite above the soil.

subsections.h3: Calculating Harvest Day and Unwatered Delays
subsections.action: Count growth days starting the day AFTER planting; daily watering is required for growth. If unwatered for a day, the crop does not die but halts growth, delaying harvest by one day.

sections.h2: How to Harvest Standard Crops by Hand
sections.title: Hand Harvesting Controls (PC Focus & Continuous Movement)
sections.purpose: Explain precise PC controls for single picking and the forum-tested hold-and-walk technique, noting general controller and mobile mappings.

subsections.action: Stand adjacent to a ripe crop. PC: Press Right-Click or X (Check/Do Action); Left-Click and C are for using tools or placing items. Controllers map to Check/Do Action (Xbox A, PS Cross, Switch A). Mobile uses generic tap to action.
On PC, holding Right-Click with the mouse cursor kept away from the character harvests the tile underfoot while walking through fields; holding seeds allows simultaneous planting and harvesting.

sections.h2: How to Harvest Designated Crops with a Scythe
sections.title: Scythe Harvesting Mechanics
sections.purpose: List verified scythe crop examples, describe tool use controls, and explain the 1.6 Iridium Scythe capability on tilled soil.

subsections.h3: Crops That Require a Scythe to Harvest
subsections.action: Equip a scythe and press the tool button (PC Left-Click/C, controller tool button, mobile select scythe then tap). Examples include Kale, Amaranth, Wheat, Unmilled Rice, and Fiber Seeds.

subsections.h3: The 1.6 Iridium Scythe Advantage on Tilled Soil
subsections.action: Obtained via 1.6 Farming Mastery, the Iridium Scythe can harvest any mature crops grown on tilled soil within its swing range, allowing wide-area scythe harvesting of standard crops.

sections.h2: Harvesting Special Crops: Giant Crops and Trellises
sections.title: Physical Crop Constraints: Giant Merges & Trellis Reachability
sections.purpose: Detail the 3-hit axe rule for harvesting giant crops and spatial planning to keep trellis crops reachable.

subsections.h3: Harvesting Giant Crops with an Axe
subsections.action: When 3x3 crops merge into a giant crop, harvest it using any axe. It takes three hits and yields 15–21 normal-quality crops. Giant crops do not wither at season change.

subsections.h3: Maintaining Reachable Paths Around Trellis Crops
subsections.action: Living trellis crops (Green Bean, Hops, Grape) cannot be walked through. Plan layouts so every trellis plant is reachable from an adjacent open tile; double-row planting with open walking aisles is a practical layout recommendation.

sections.title: Diagnosing Common Harvest Blockers
sections.purpose: Help reader quickly resolve specific obstacles preventing harvest without repeating the full guide.
